posts.author: John Klayer
posts.content_md: I see a 10 mW 473nm blue dpss on eBay. If the coherence length is okay, would 10 mW of 473nm be enough for reasonable exposure times in DCG?

posts.author: edelbrp
posts.content_md:
Looking at the PFG-04 specs, it looks like blue is much more sensitive:

[http://www.geola.com/holomaterials_pfg04.htm](http://www.geola.com/holomaterials_pfg04.htm)

Not sure how this would apply to the roll-your-own DCG.

Is this it?

[http://cgi.ebay.com/ws/eBayISAPI.dll?Vi ... eName=WDVW](http://cgi.ebay.com/ws/eBayISAPI.dll?ViewItem&category=26237&item=3846351898&rd=1&ssPageName=WDVW)

I'd be wary of this laser. No coherence length specs and the seller sells mostly laser show items and modified laser pointers. Feedback of seller is 99.0% positive, which actually isn't super. Some negative feedback include wrong laser specs.

-Phil

posts.author: Sergio
posts.content_md:
The laser seems designed to scientific use:

# Raman Spectroscopy

# DNA sequencing

# Cell assorting

# Fluorsecence spectroscopy

# Biomedical instrumentation

# Laser display

# Laser interference

# Holography

# Wafer inspection

Raman and fluorescent spectroscopy requires narrow linewidth, I guess, even with a 1cm coherence it may be an inportant laser for colour holography..

.
